original.target_description: Study 1: question-level quadratic relation between mean trajectory sample entropy and distance from equibiased truth probability (.5); middle-truth-value questions versus low- and high-truth-value questions, Fig. 1d and entropy results.

n.sample_role: Question-level observations (mean trajectory sample entropy for each question), based on responses from 141 participants.
n.exclusions: No question-level exclusions reported. The 54 participants with reversed response positions were retained after mirror reversal.
n.location: Printed p. 22 Method; printed p. 23 Fig. 1d caption; printed p. 24 entropy results (PDF pp. 1–3).
n.quote: The data for this study come from 141 college-age participants ... (97 females, 44 males) who responded to 11 yes/no questions ... The graph in (d) plots the mean sample entropy of trajectories for each question ... as a function of distance from equibiased probability (.5);

es.location: Printed p. 24, left column, sample entropy paragraph (PDF p. 3); Fig. 1d, printed p. 23.
es.quote: Sample entropy was higher for middle-truth-value questions ... than for low- and high-truth-value questions (see Fig. 1d), ... quadratic r 5 .70, F(1, 9) 5 8.7, p < .05, prep 5 .939.

notes: Only assigned n_o and es_value_o completed; replication, p and reported-success fields are unassigned placeholders. Target is the sample-entropy comparison on printed p. 24 (PDF p. 3), linked explicitly to Fig. 1d on p. 23. Analytic units are the 11 questions, each represented by mean trajectory sample entropy; 141 is the participant source sample, not the number of question-level observations in this correlation. N is supported by the explicit 11-question method and per-question figure caption, not calculated from F degrees of freedom. No group sum or other arithmetic performed. No exclusions are described for this question-level entropy analysis. The 54 reversed-response participants were mirror-reversed and retained, not excluded. PDF p. 3 visibly prints quadratic r = −.70; the canonical text omits the minus sign and substitutes 5 for equals. The effect value retains the PDF minus sign while the quote reproduces the canonical text literally. Same-test printed F(1, 9) = 8.7, p < .05, p_rep = .939; p_rep is not the significance p. No conversion to another effect metric.
